notice: Engram is a third-party MIT program (Gentleman-Programming/engram). PiCode ships its engine unchanged: the name and logo are its author's trademarks, so no surface here is dressed as their product.
note: The pinned memory engine, fetched from its own release by build/engram-runtime.sh and carried at `<pack>/resources/memory/engram.exe`. Pinned, never `latest`: an editor built today must behave the same in six months, and the store it writes is shared with whatever other agent on the machine points at `~/.engram` — a version that moves on its own is a version that can migrate somebody else's memory without asking. 3.6.2 follows 3.6.0 (the first step past 3.5.1, the release the owner already ran): 3.6.1 hardens soft deletes against stale snapshots and folds accents in search, and 3.6.2 only lines the engine up with gentle-engram 0.6.0. Like 3.6.0, its changes carry no store migration, so PiCode keeps joining the store it has rather than opening a second one on it. It is the `gentle-engram` pi package is pinned separately in the profile (product-packages.ts) and pointed at this engine through ENGRAM_BIN.
